comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of anion-binding site folding/unfolding coupled to Cl⁻ binding (C7-C9, C45-C46, C55-C56, C70-C71). OpenEval emphasizes HDX-MS experimental convergence and reversibility; peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as convincing evidence with thermodynamic validation (C72). Peer review includes C72 while OpenEval separates it into R17.

Perfect agreement on comparative findings between prestin and SLC26A9 (C10, C42-C44, C49, C51-C52). Both evaluations find the quantitative differences (100-fold stability, 20-fold HDX changes) convincing evidence that prestin's unique dynamics underlie its motor function versus SLC26A9's transporter role.

Complete agreement on nanodisc vs. micelle comparison (C12, C60-C61, C69). Both accept the TM6 destabilization finding and its relevance to lipid bilayer environment. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of thorough investigation without challenge; OpenEval notes strong quantitative evidence (10-fold HDX increase).

Both support helix fraying findings (C14, C62-C63, C65, C76), but peer review R4 encompasses broader cooperativity claims (C15-C16, C64, C66-C68, C77-C78) that OpenEval separates into R5, R6, and R18. Peer reviewers strongly praise the cooperativity analysis as providing evidence for fast electromechanical rearrangement; OpenEval finds C76 reasonable but somewhat speculative.

OpenEval R5 addresses cooperativity analysis (C15, C64, C66-C68, C81) that peer reviewers group with helix fraying in R4. Both find the quantitative cooperativity metrics (σΔG values) well-supported. OpenEval separates this from helix fraying (R4) while peer review treats them together as integrated evidence.

Both evaluate mechanistic proposals linking dynamics to function (C16, C78, C82), but with different emphasis. OpenEval finds these speculative hypotheses requiring validation; peer reviewers note interpretations would benefit from orthogonal evidence (MD simulations suggested) and find the voltage-dependent mechanism 'a bit speculative.' Agreement on uncertain status.

Divergent evaluations of region-specific stability patterns (C53-C54, C73). OpenEval finds these supported by HDX-MS data and consistent with elevator-like mechanism; peer reviewer R6 questions the functional interpretation, finding it unclear how cytosolic similarities contribute to differential TMD mechanisms. Disagreement on interpretation clarity.

Divergent evaluations of allosteric modulation by different anions (C58, C74-C75). OpenEval finds claims supported by HDX data with different anions, though C75 somewhat speculative; peer reviewer R5 finds the allosteric mechanism unclear without chloride titration experiments, questioning how allostery works with only extreme conditions shown.

Complete agreement on Pro136 sequence conservation and functional significance (C79-C80). Both accept the sequence alignment data and cited experimental evidence without challenge. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as supporting evidence for prestin's unique structural basis.

Both support cryo-EM structural findings (C83-C84). OpenEval finds the Cl⁻-bound interpretation reasonable based on density analysis and binding fraction calculations; peer reviewers accept structural observations without challenge as validation of system robustness. Peer R10 also includes C85-C86 that OpenEval separates into R12.

Perfect agreement on experimental design and conditions (C40-C41). Both accept the two-condition approach and EX2 kinetics determination as standard and well-executed. Peer reviewers praise experiments as well-designed with quality allowing quantitative interpretation.

OpenEval R12 addresses structural comparison across sources (C85-C86) that peer reviewers include in R10 with cryo-EM findings. Both support these comparisons as validating system robustness. Agreement on structural reproducibility supporting HDX interpretation.

OpenEval R17 separately evaluates thermodynamic validation (C72) comparing measured vs. calculated ΔΔG values; peer reviewers include this in R1 as part of core folding evidence. Both find the agreement between measured and calculated values supportive. Organizational difference only.

OpenEval R18 evaluates multi-state barrier speculation (C77) as uncertain; peer reviewers include this claim in R4 with helix fraying evidence. Both treat the kinetic barrier connection as speculative, though peer review emphasizes the overall cooperativity analysis strength while OpenEval isolates this specific speculation.

OpenEval R1 includes urea and titration experiments (C56-C57) as part of core folding evidence; peer reviewers separately evaluate these in R7 as supporting reversibility. Both find the evidence supportive; difference is organizational grouping.
OpenEval R13 evaluates background literature claims (C1-C4, C17-C24) as supported context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not separately assess background claims.
OpenEval R14 evaluates prior structural work summary (C25-C32) as supported background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not separately assess literature context claims.

OpenEval R15 evaluates prior functional/computational work (C33-C39) as supported background establishing mechanistic context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focus on novel findings rather than literature summaries.

OpenEval R16 evaluates additional background claims (C5-C6, C13, C87-C90) as supported context from prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not separately assess these contextual claims.
